newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock index futures end mostly lower.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock index futures end mostly lower.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures ended mostly lower, with March Standard & Poor's 500s grudgingly correcting record gains after a topsy-turvy day of modest pit trade, traders said.

As usual, the heaviest selling pressure of the session was generated after U.S. bond futures closed for the day at 1400 CST/2000 GMT. Sharp down- or up-moves have recently been staged in the latter half of the day, several analysts noted.
They said the U.S. bond market's performance on Wednesday was disappointing, given the positive U.S. January consumer price index and January real earnings reports.

Both reports suggested inflationary pressures in the U.S. economy remained low. Both the overall CPI and core rate rose 0.1 percent, lower than average trade estimates for up 0.3 percent and up 0.2 percent, respectively.
Meanwhile, real earnings fell 2.0 percent in January, the biggest drop since August 1973.
Despite the bond market's weakness, March S&Ps rallied to 820.20 and later popped to 820.40, an all-time high.
Later in the afternoon, arbitrage sell programs were enacted in the afternoon after two major U.S. firms turned into aggressive sellers in the pit.
Arbitrage sell programs were noted at a premium of 1.60 to 1.75 points over the cash index, several floor sources said. Fair value was at 2.23 to 2.29 points to cash.
"Locals had to chase the market down," one trader said, adding that volume was modest on both the up- and down-side.
March S&Ps fell to 812.50, through support at 814.00 and below the pivot point of 812.75.

At the end of pit trade, March S&Ps were down 4.05 at 814.30, KCBT Value Lines were 2.50 lower at 719.10, NYSE Composites were down 2.25 at 426.35, Nikkeis were up 100.0 at 18,600, Midcap 400s were down 0.10 at 269.70 and Nasdaq 100s were down 1.50 at 900.00.
